chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Baghdadi, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-Ja'fari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It is written in the Torah: 'Thank the one who bestows favor upon you, and bestow favor upon the one who thanks you, for there is no decline of the bounties when they are thanked for, and there is no permanence for them when they are denied. Gratitude is an increase in the bounties and a safety from changes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of gratitude according to the Torah as cited in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the concept of 'Shukr al-Ni'ma' (gratitude for blessings) by citing a verse from the Torah, illustrating the Shia tradition of drawing wisdom from previous scriptures. It establishes that gratitude serves as both a mechanism for increasing divine favor and a safeguard against sudden changes in fortune, while ingratitude inevitably leads to the loss of blessings.
